heroHeadline: Israeli Forces Shoot Four Palestinians Guarding Settler Raid Near Ramallah as Netanyahu's Rare Condemnation of Settler Violence Goes Unheeded
heroSubtitle: Over August 29–31, 2026, masked settlers attacked an NBC News crew and resident Aida Ahmed Abdullah in Jalud and stormed a home in Qusra, prompting Prime Minister Netanyahu to break his silence and condemn 'criminal acts of violence' by 'a handful of rioters.' The condemnation had little practical effect: on August 30, settlers attacked al-Mughayyir village and accompanying IDF troops fired live ammunition, wounding four young men, while on August 31 IDF soldiers guarding a separate settler operation near Ramallah shot and wounded four more Palestinians, including two minors, and settlers beat a woman and child in Burqa. Israeli police separately asked a court for arrest warrants against settlers involved in the Qusra home takeover. In Gaza, Israeli strikes killed at least 9 Palestinians over the same three days: 2 in Deir al-Balah on August 29 (a Hamas commander struck at the Shuhada al-Aqsa Hospital compound plus 3 more nearby, including Hamouda al-Attar), a 3-year-old boy and one other near a Deir al-Balah bakery on August 30, and 5 more in two separate Gaza City strikes on August 31 near the municipal public park and in the Tel al-Hawa neighborhood. The cumulative Palestinian death toll in Gaza since October 7, 2023 now exceeds 73,430+, with more than 1,300 killed since the October 2025 ceasefire took effect.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OCHA, IDF, Gaza Ministry of Health, B'Tselem, ICC, ICJ, Reuters, Al Jazeera, OHCHR, UNRWA, Times of Israel, Haaretz, Bloomberg, Jerusalem Post, Human Rights Watch, Save the Children, Amnesty International, UNICEF, NPR, Middle East Eye, CNN, The National, Euronews, CBC News, NBC News, FDD, WFP, PBS NewsHour, Courthouse News, and institutional analyses. Casualty figures are subject to ongoing verification. The conflict has persisted since Israeli independence on May 14, 1948.
